newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian dlr regains poise after rate cut rumour.
newsitem.headline: Australian dlr regains poise after rate cut rumour.

text.p: The Australian dollar recovered from an early scare of a rumoured rate cut to be testing a key resistance level, with traders saying the market remained short and the near term bias was for further gains.

Rumours of a rate cut, said to have come from a U.S investment bank that had been an active buyer of the dollar through the week, sparked a heavy sell off that pushed the dollar through US$0.7400 to a low of US$0.7387/92.
However, when the bank denied the rumours, and no rate cut was forthcoming, the dollar rallied strongly through a number of resistance levels to reach a high of US$0.7443/48.
By 5.00 p.m. (0700 GMT), the dollar was steadying at US$0.7430/35, up on an early US$0.7409/14 and basically level with Thursday's local close of US$0.7436/41.
"Basically, it was probably a false break," said one trader of the early morning fall, adding that while the rally towards US$0.7450 was probably overdone, the dollar remained well supported.
"The real buyers actually pulled away at that US$0.7405/10 area when all the (rate cut) rumours started, and I think they re-entered and now they've still got the demand and the interest."

The market was confused by the fact that the bank said to be calling for a rate cut and selling the local dollar this morning had been a keen buyer of the dollar all week, and emerged as a buyer at the lows and remained a buyer on dips through the day. With the currency holding up well in the face of the rate cut rumour, and after Thursday's sharp fall from a two week high of US$0.7483, it was expected to continue to edge higher.

"I think there's still some demand out there," the trader said. "Yesterday was just a bit of a clean out, and basically we've probably going to see a little bit of a bid bias over the next couple of days."
With little on the local data calendar until late in the month, attention is expected to remain on interest rates in the lead up to next week's U.S. FOMC meeting.
Caution ahead of the meeting, on the outside chance the U.S. lifts rates, is seen capping the dollar under US$0.75 in the near term.
On the crosses, the Australian dollar continued to improve against the yen on the back of U.S dollar strength.
The U.S. dollar has risen on concerns the yen may have to weaken to maintain Japanese competitiveness in export markets following the recent Asian currency turmoil.
The Indonesian rupiah hit a new low on Friday, one day after it moved to a managed float, with the Malaysian ringgit and Singapore dollar also weakening.

The Australian dollar ended at 87/86/96 yen from an opening 87.39/49 and a close on Thursday of 86.35/45. In trade weighted terms the dollar closed at 58.9, up on an opening 58.4 and a Thursday close of 58.5.
